chunks: ‘Alī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام said: “If my slave steals from me, I do not amputate him; and if my slave steals from someone other than me, I amputate him. And the slave of the imārah, if he steals, I do not amputate him, because he is fay’.”

key_terms.أَقْطَعْهُ: I amputate him; meaning I apply the hadd penalty of theft
key_terms.سَرَقَنِي: stole from me; theft directed against the owner himself
key_terms.عَبْدُ الْإِمَارَةِ: the slave belonging to the governing authority or public administration
key_terms.غَيْرِي: someone other than me; another person besides the owner
key_terms.فَيْءٌ: public property or state-held property returned to the Muslim polity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave steals from his master or if a state-owned slave steals?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning theft by a privately owned slave and by a slave belonging to the public authority. It distinguishes between theft from one’s own property and theft from the property of others, and it also treats the slave of the imārah differently because such a slave is considered part of the public fay’.
